purpose: One coherent BACE interface across three states; static concepts, not an implemented interaction.
authorization: The author explicitly approved Canva with illustrative data; authorization carried forward to the requested revision.

frames.reference_role: Rejected density and layout, retained only as subject context
frames.prompt:
Create a realistic production-quality UI SCREENSHOT for BACE, a desktop evidence-assessment research application. One screenshot, one application state. Target 1440 x 1024, natural desktop viewport; no browser chrome, no phone, no perspective, no surrounding presentation board. Current date anchor 2026-10-22. Report year 2023 is a deliberate historical demo. All visible text English.

The approved design direction is a calm DOCUMENT-CENTERED experience with progressive disclosure. The author found the earlier permanent three-pane screens crowded and tiring. Make this substantially easier to read. The reading surface is the hero, UI chrome recedes. No left navigation sidebar, no permanent claim list, no workflow ribbon, no metrics cards, no nested cards, no shadow stacks, no colorful background panels, no decorative illustrations or charts. Place only information required for the current state. References in principle: iA Writer's text-led surface, Readwise's optional panels, Notion's on-demand side peek, Linear's quiet navigation and restrained separators. These are principles, not a request to copy branding.

CONSISTENT VISUAL SYSTEM for every state: warm white #FAFAF8 page, white detail surface when present, deep ink #202725 text, secondary text #657069 with readable contrast, forest green #235A47 as the sole action/selection accent, restrained amber only for an Unsupported label. Source prose in a very readable restrained serif (Source Serif 4 or equivalent), body size 19-20 px at 1440px canvas, line height 1.65; UI text Inter or equivalent 15-16 px. Page title 32 px serif. Keep comfortable line length, no microtype. Header height about 68px, text wordmark BACE aligned left at x48, case context 'Example Manufacturing / 2023' in the header, quiet label 'Illustrative data'. Thin line below header. Secondary row with text tabs Disclosure (active) and Evidence. Main content starts about y190. Use generous 32-48px vertical separation and real empty space. No oversized decorative headline.

DEMO DATA, not experimental results: disclosure title 'Climate disclosure'. Subtitle 'Example Manufacturing · Reporting year 2023'. EXACT DISCLOSURE text, as two paragraphs:
'Scope 1 emissions decreased by 20% between 2022 and 2023.'
'All manufacturing sites used renewable electricity in 2023.'
Only these two claims. Outcome summary, if used, must be '1 supported · 1 unsupported'.
DC-01 is first sentence, Supported · Inferred. Candidate EC-01 'Scope 1 emissions were 100,000 tCO2e in 2022.' Candidate EC-02 'Scope 1 emissions were 80,000 tCO2e in 2023.' Accepted Set A requires EC-01 AND EC-02 jointly; neither is individually sufficient. These two ECs are the full candidate set for DC-01. Support type inferred does not imply a saved prose rationale. Do not invent a rationale or confidence score.
DC-02 is second sentence, Unsupported. Candidate EC-03: 'The pilot facility used renewable electricity in 2023.' No accepted support set. Diagnosis 'Factual boundary distortion'. Illustrative explanation: 'The evidence covers the pilot facility; the disclosure expands this to all manufacturing sites.'
Source titles: 'Example evidence A', 'Example evidence B', 'Example evidence C'. This is synthetic visual demo data, not actual BACE model output. No external company facts. Keep a visible Illustrative data label.
Do not call candidates verified, rejected, or supporting merely from selection. No trust score, legal compliance, model confidence, chat assistant, or invented timeline.
STATE: READ DISCLOSURE. Use one centered reading column roughly 700px wide, starting x370. No detail panel is open. Title, subtitle, two generous short paragraphs form one calm page. Place tiny unobtrusive margin markers beside the two paragraphs, with very short 'Supported' and 'Unsupported' text markers in the margin (not large colored boxes). No claim IDs or EC texts anywhere on this initial screen. Under title, understated '1 supported · 1 unsupported'. Above body a quiet text action 'All claims'. Below body ONE forest-green button 'Review unsupported' and one quiet secondary link 'View process'. At the bottom of the content a short subtle instruction 'Select a claim to inspect its evidence.' Abundant surrounding whitespace. The supplied image reference is the REJECTED earlier dense design: use it only to understand the subject and what to remove. Do NOT preserve its three columns, typography density, permanent list, or panel layout. This new reading screen must be radically quieter and text-led.

Keep the full original disclosure visible on the LEFT in a wide readable column around 640px. The title and prose keep the same vertical reading position as the reference; move the reading region left gently to make room. Highlight ONLY the second sentence with a pale amber underline and slim margin marker. Keep the first paragraph dark and readable. No claim inventory or third column.

On the RIGHT, show a single plain white inspector about 400-430px wide, separated by one subtle vertical divider. No extra cards enclosing the whole panel. Header 'Claim details' and visible close icon. Contents in this exact reading order: small amber 'Unsupported' label; full selected claim 'All manufacturing sites used renewable electricity in 2023.' as a 20px multiline heading; label 'Factual boundary distortion'; explanation 'The evidence covers the pilot facility; the disclosure expands this to all manufacturing sites.' Set explanation in readable 16px type with generous space.
Below one light divider: 'Evidence considered', then one source line 'Example evidence C', then quotation 'The pilot facility used renewable electricity in 2023.' A quiet line reads 'No accepted support set'. The main green action is 'View source'; secondary text action 'View trace'. Bottom simple Previous claim and Next claim navigation or 'Claim 2 of 2'. Include the full recorded demo content, but no raw IDs, confidence score, full taxonomy or metadata table. The current result should be understandable by reading the right panel top-to-bottom.
